entries.claim: low-pass filtering after ring modulation suppresses brittle high-frequency products while preserving the sum-and-difference structure
entries.what: A product signal followed by a low-pass stage, with the cutoff chosen against the new spectrum rather than inherited from either input. The multiplication still creates sum-and-difference components; the following stage decides how much of their upper, brittle region remains.
entries.why: Multiplication creates components above and below the input frequencies, often adding a dense high-frequency edge. Filtering the result acts on those newly created components. Filtering either input first is not equivalent because it changes which products are created in the first place.

listen_for.sounds_like: an inharmonic or metallic structure whose identity remains clear without the upper edge dominating it
listen_for.confusable_with: filtering before multiplication, which changes the ingredients and therefore changes the product spectrum itself

entries.source: Allen Strange, Electronic Music: Systems, Techniques and Controls, a worked ring-modulator filtering example

anchor.shows: A worked signal path placing a low-pass stage after a ring modulator and explaining the intended spectral restraint.

evidence.shows: A worked signal path placing a low-pass stage after a ring modulator and explaining the intended spectral restraint.

validation.off: Generate with the admitted knowledge loader, which excludes this candidate.

controls: Use the same installed inventory, generator model, attempt count and audibility gate.
Require ring modulation and an audible output in both arms; reject topology changes that replace the requested technique.
Keep every generated patch and compare paired attempts rather than selecting only the best on-arm result.
measure: Blind listening for retained metallic identity with reduced brittle high-frequency dominance.
Quality Lab spectral_centroid and hf_fizz as corroboration, guarded against regressions in audibility and spectral_flux.
validation.promotion: Admit only if the guided arm wins the blinded paired comparison and Pareto-improves the stated detectors without losing the requested ring-modulated identity.
